findings.title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting() defeats the $__range guard and splits range-variable queries incorrectly
findings.body: runSplitQuery() now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables() on each target (line 299) before the queries are partitioned by querySupportsSplitting() (line 300). That function excludes queries containing $__range/$__range_ms/$_interval etc. via isQueryWithRangeVariable() precisely so they are NOT time-split (see the comment at lines 285-288: these variables are meant to be resolved by the backend against each sub-request's split time range). applyTemplateVariables runs templateSrv.replace with request.scopedVars, and panel/Explore requests include built-ins like __range in scopedVars, so a query such as count_over_time({a="b"}[$__range]) is rewritten to a fixed full-range duration (e.g. [2d]) before the guard runs. The guard then no longer matches, the query is classified as splittable and split into 1-day chunks, each of which evaluates a 2-day window: the chunks overlap, data is double-counted, and the combined result is wrong. Before this change these queries were sent as a single unsplit request. Either the range-variable check must run on the pre-interpolation expr, or interpolation must preserve/skip the built-in range variables.

findings.title: Shard-split queries are template-interpolated twice
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery() now applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables() to every target (line 52), and those interpolated targets are later passed as subRequest.targets into runSplitQuery() (line 163), which - after this same PR - applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables() again on each of them (querySplitting.ts line 299). The result is that every shard-split query is interpolated twice. Double interpolation is not idempotent: a literal escaped dollar written as $$var becomes $var after the first pass and is then expanded to the variable's value by the second pass, and variable values that themselves contain $ or text matching another variable name get re-expanded. Previously interpolation happened exactly once (via interpolateVariablesInQueries in runShardSplitQuery, with runSplitQuery doing none). The updated tests don't catch this because the mocked applyTemplateVariables only does a no-op-on-second-pass string replace. runShardSplitQuery should either skip its own interpolation now that runSplitQuery interpolates, or runSplitQuery needs a way to know the targets are already interpolated.

findings.title: No regression test that $__range queries are still excluded from splitting after interpolation
findings.body: The only new test ('Interpolates queries before execution') covers $__auto/$step interpolation, but there is no test asserting that a query using $__range (or another range variable) is still routed to the non-splitting group now that interpolation happens before the querySupportsSplitting()/isQueryWithRangeVariable() check in runSplitQuery. Since that guard inspects the raw expr for the literal $__range token and the new interpolation step can remove that token, a test pinning the 'queries with $__range are not split' behavior is needed to catch the regression; without it, the wrong-results scenario for range-variable queries ships silently.
